PCI and PCI VS CABG and medical therapy\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EReference from:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK556123\/\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EPrimary PCI is the recommended method of reperfusion when it can be performed in a timely fashion by experienced operators\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESTEMI and ischemic symptoms of less than 12 hours' duration\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESTEMI and ischemic symptoms of less than 12 hours' duration and contraindications to fibrinolytic therapy\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EReference from:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK556123\/\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPercutaneous coronary intervention is being used extensively over the last many years. 80% of PCI is being done with stents. Over the past 20 years, short-term mortality, MI, and target vessel revascularization have shown a significant reduction in patients with PCI.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EComparing the outcomes in different trials for PCI vs. CABG and medical therapy, the following are the preferred treatments for different patient categories.\u0026nbsp;SYNTAX score is a tool used to estimate the complexity of coronary lesions and helps determine the decision-making process between PCI or CABG.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPCI vs. CABG\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECABG is preferred in patients with two or three-vessel disease.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECABG is also preferred in patients with the left main disease or one or two-vessel disease and low SYNTAX score.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECABG has shown better outcomes with multivessel disease in patients with diabetes compared with PCI\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPCI vs. Medical Therapy\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EMedical therapy with high-dose statins is preferred over balloon angioplasty in patients with mild anginal symptoms.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EPCI is preferred over medical therapy if the patient has;\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESevere symptoms\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EFailed medical therapy\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EHigh-risk coronary anatomy\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EWorsening LV function\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4.How vaccum assisted closure is useful?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EReference from\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.hopkinsmedicine.org\/health\/treatment-tests-and-therapies\/vacuumassisted-closure-of-a-wound\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe gases in the air around us put pressure on the surface of our bodies. A wound vacuum device removes this pressure over the area of the wound. This can help a wound heal in several ways. It can gently pull fluid from the wound over time. This can reduce swelling, and may help clean the wound and remove bacteria. A wound VAC also helps pull the edges of the wound together. And it may stimulate the growth of new tissue that helps the wound close.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA wound vacuum system has several parts. A foam or gauze dressing is put directly on the wound. An adhesive film covers and seals the dressing and wound. A drainage tube leads from under the adhesive film and connects to a portable vacuum pump. This pump removes air pressure over the wound. It may does this either constantly. Or it may do it in cycles.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe dressing is changed every 24 to 72 hours.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUses:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDraining excess fluid from the wound\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EReducing swelling\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EReducing bacteria in the wound\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EKeeping your wound moist and warm\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHelping draw together wound edges\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIncreasing blood flow to your wound\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDecreasing redness and swelling (inflammation)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5) Role of adipokines in CAD\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EReference
